Five-class tau PET framework detects more early pathology

Implementation-relevant•Peer-reviewed prospective multicenter cross-sectional validation study•September 21, 2026

Five-class tau PET framework detects more early pathology

In 681 participants, a five-class visual framework achieved interrater kappa values of 0.77 to 0.85 and classified more cognitively unimpaired and MCI participants as tau-positive than the FDA-approved flortaucipir binary read, but the new framework itself is not authorized or guideline-endorsed and has no proven clinical utility.

Key quantitative results: Interrater agreement for the five classes was kappa 0.77 to 0.85. Intertracer agreement was highest for MK-6240 versus flortaucipir (kappa 0.88); across all tracer pairs, five-class percentage agreement ranged from 75.2% to 83.3%.

BiomarkersTau PETTau tanglesAmyloidTau pathology staging

Added September 22, 2026 · DOI:10.1001/jamaneurol.2026.3253; PMID:42766299

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The harmonized approach moves tau PET beyond a late-stage binary read and provides a common vocabulary across four tracers. It increases early-stage positivity and tracks with cognition and other biomarkers, but the same cohort was used to develop and evaluate it, and no prospective decision-impact or outcome study has established clinical utility.

Study design

The HEAD study enrolled adults aged 50 to 90 years at nine North American and European sites. The analysis included 681 participants (369 cognitively unimpaired, 245 with MCI and 67 with dementia) who underwent two to four tau PET scans, amyloid PET, MRI and cognitive assessment. Blinded readers assigned negative, low, moderate, high or atypical classes from seven composite regions.

Key quantitative results

  • Interrater agreement for the five classes was kappa 0.77 to 0.85. Intertracer agreement was highest for MK-6240 versus flortaucipir (kappa 0.88); across all tracer pairs, five-class percentage agreement ranged from 75.2% to 83.3%.
  • Among cognitively unimpaired participants, the FDA-approved flortaucipir binary read was positive in 26/364, versus 49/364 with harmonized flortaucipir (prevalence ratio 1.89, 95% CI 1.31 to 2.70) and 71/364 with harmonized MK-6240 (2.73, 1.95 to 3.83). In MCI, the corresponding counts were 100/223, 123/223 (1.23, 1.12 to 1.35) and 142/223 (1.42, 1.27 to 1.59).
  • From low to high tau classes, cognition was 1.4-fold worse, amyloid PET burden 3.2-fold higher and plasma p-tau217 2.5-fold higher; positivity estimates converged in dementia at 45/57, 47/57 and 50/57 for the regulatory, harmonized flortaucipir and harmonized MK-6240 reads.

What changed

A peer-reviewed prospective multicenter study now provides a reproducible five-class visual staging framework across four tau PET tracers and quantifies how much more early-stage pathology it detects than the approved flortaucipir binary read.

Strength of evidence

Strong agreement and convergent clinical-validity evidence within a large head-to-head imaging cohort. Analytical validity and reader reproducibility were not established outside the study, the framework was developed and evaluated in the same cohort, and longitudinal prognostic and decision-impact validation are still needed.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

The framework may improve research staging and trial enrichment, especially before dementia, but it should not be substituted for an approved tracer's labeled read or used alone for treatment decisions until externally validated and implemented under appropriate guidance.

Field medical relevance

Directly relevant to imaging interpretation, biological staging and blood-biomarker studies that use tau PET as a reference. It also shows that tracer and reading method can change apparent positivity in early disease.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The method uses tracer-specific images but a common seven-region, five-class visual scheme. Agreement was strongest for MK-6240 and flortaucipir, and performance was lower for some regions with PI-2620, so tracer equivalence should not be assumed.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No new authorization, commercial availability, guideline endorsement, coverage or reimbursement follows from the framework. A free research visual-reading tool is available, but access to tracers, scanners and trained readers remains separate.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Is this five-class read FDA approved?
No. Tauvid and Tauklarify are approved tracers with their own labeled visual-read methods; this harmonized framework is a research method and has no separate authorization.
Does greater positivity prove better diagnosis or outcomes?
No. The study supports agreement and association with disease measures, but it did not establish that the additional early positives improve decisions, outcomes or treatment selection.
Can results be treated as interchangeable across tracers?
No. Agreement was good to excellent overall but varied by tracer and region, and atypical classifications did not converge across tracers.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Framework development and evaluation occurred in the same cohort without external validation
  • Cross-sectional design without longitudinal prognostic or treatment-response assessment
  • Smaller RO948 and PI-2620 samples and lower regional confidence for PI-2620
  • Predominantly highly educated White non-Hispanic academic-research cohort
  • No neuropathology reference standard, decision-impact study or clinical-utility evaluation
